metadata.title: Forbes 400 Adds Record 10 Billionaires Under 40 Amid AI Wealth Surge

sources.news_title: Forbes releases list of top 400 wealthiest people in America: Who's the richest in each state?

sources.text:
Forbes reports:
With the AI and data center boom in full swing and the U.S. stock market near an all-time high, it now takes a record $4.4 billion to rank among the nation’s 400 wealthiest people. That’s $600 million more than last year and $2.7 billion more than a decade ago. In all, this year’s Forbes 400 is richer than ever, worth a combined $8 trillion, up from $6.6 trillion in 2025.
Overall, the 20 very richest people in America have gotten nearly $1 trillion richer over the past year; as a group, they are now worth a record $4 trillion. Fifteen of them are centibillionaires, meaning someone with a net worth of at least $100 billion. Forbes calculated net worths using share prices from September 4, 2026.
Despite the record high bar for entry, 34 newcomers managed to wrest a spot on the list. Among the new faces are more than a dozen artificial intelligence moguls, including the youngest newcomer, 30-year-old Cognition AI cofounder Steven Hao ($5.8 billion); six cofounders of Claude developer Anthropic (estimated net worths: $15.5 billion each), including Daniela Amodei, who is now the second richest self-made woman in the nation; and Greg Brockman, the cofounder of ChatGPT giant OpenAI, who is the richest newcomer of all this year, worth an estimated $25.5 billion.
Read the full article. There’s much more. No paywall.

JACKSONVILLE, Fla. — Jacksonville Jaguars owner Shad Khan remains one of the richest people in America, according to Forbes’ 2026 ranking of the 400 Richest People in America.
On this year’s list, Khan was ranked No. 70 with a net worth of $16.5 billion. In 2025, Khan was ranked No. 74 with a net worth of $14.3 billion.
Khan paid $770 million for the Jaguars in 2011. In June 2024, the Jacksonville City Council approved a $1.4 billion deal for the Stadium of the Future renovations at EverBank Stadium. Those renovations are set to be completed by the beginning of the 2028 season.
Among NFL owners, five ranked ahead of Khan.
Rob Walton, Denver Broncos owner, and his family were ranked at No. 11 with a worth of $132 billion.
David Tepper, owner of the Carolina Panthers, was ranked at No. 39 with a worth of $28.5 billion.
Stanley Kroenke, the owner of the Los Angeles Rams, came in at No. 41 with a worth of $27.6 billion.
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones and his family came in at No. 49 with a worth of $23.5 billion.
Stephen Ross, owner of the Miami Dolphins, came in at No. 56 with a net worth of $21.5 billion.
New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft (No. 81, $15.2 billion)
Atlanta Falcons owner Arthur Blank (No. 99, $13.2 billion)
Josh Harris, manager of the Washington Commanders ownership group (No. 109, $12.4 billion)
Cleveland Browns owner Jimmy Haslam (No. 114, $12.2 billion)
New Orleans Saints owner Gayle Benson (No. 139, $11.2 billion)
Philadelphia Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie and his family (No. 187, $8.8 billion)
Cincinnati Bengals owner Mike Brown and his family (No. 224, $7.6 billion)
Khan, 75, first made his fortune as the owner of an auto parts company called Flex-N-Gate.
In 2013, he added to his sports ownership portfolio, buying Fulham FC, a soccer club in England.

The combined wealth of the 400 richest people in the United States has reached a record $8 trillion, an increase of 1.4 trillion over the year, according to the Forbes magazine rating.
Only 20 people account for half of this amount — $4 trillion. Elon Musk (Tesla, SpaceX) is in the lead with a fortune of $ 908 billion, followed by Jeff Bezos (Amazon) with $ 378 billion and Larry Page (Google) with $ 278 billion. Getting into the rating now requires at least 4.4 billion dollars.
